issues.legal_issue: A transferee who failed to raise and substantiate an objection before the original authority cannot obtain a fresh inquiry merely because an appellate authority examined a suspicious land record.
material_facts: The transferees’ representative was present and heard by the original authority, but the specific objections later advanced were not raised there or adequately pleaded in the appeal.
The appellate authority examined the land record on its own initiative and found features that raised doubts about its authenticity.

The transferees did not ask for the record-keeper to be summoned to explain those features and did not provide an adequate reason for their failure to raise the objections or produce supporting evidence earlier.
issues.conclusion: There was no justification for remanding the matter for a fresh inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: A Khasra Girdawri is admissible under Section 35 of the Evidence Act, 1872, but it does not receive the statutory presumption of correctness that Section 44 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act gives to records of rights and Jamabandis. The optional presumption under Section 114, Illustration (c), of the Evidence Act does not apply where the record appears suspicious. An appellate authority’s examination of such a record as a matter of caution does not entitle a party that failed to raise its case earlier to demand a fresh inquiry.

rule.if: appeal_from_surplus_area_determination and specific_objection_not_raised_before_original_authority and suspicious_land_record and not record_keeper_explanation_requested and no_adequate_reason_for_late_evidence

predicates.appeal_from_surplus_area_determination: The proceeding was an appeal challenging a determination of surplus agricultural land.
predicates.specific_objection_not_raised_before_ori: The transferees did not raise the specific objection before the authority that first determined the surplus area.
predicates.suspicious_land_record: The appellate authority found features in the land record that raised doubts about its authenticity.
predicates.record_keeper_explanation_requested: The transferees requested that the record-keeper be summoned to explain the questionable features of the record.
predicates.no_adequate_reason_for_late_evidence: The transferees gave no adequate reason for failing to raise their objection or produce supporting evidence earlier.
predicates.fresh_inquiry_not_required: The matter need not be sent back for a fresh inquiry.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a surplus-land determination, a party that did not raise its specific objection before the original authority and cannot adequately explain its late evidence is not entitled to a fresh inquiry based on a suspicious land record, particularly when it did not request an explanation from the record-keeper.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee is not entitled to have purchased land placed in the transferor’s permissible area merely because the transfer occurred before that area was fixed.
material_facts: The landowner did not reserve or select a permissible area within the prescribed time, so the authority determined the permissible and surplus areas.
The land had been transferred before the permissible area was fixed.
The authority heard the parties and considered the allocation of the transferred land.
The transferees did not provide particulars of their purchases or oppose the landowner’s preference concerning the allocation of the transferred land.
issues.conclusion: The authority was not required to include the transferred land in the landowner’s permissible area; it could allocate the land to the permissible or surplus area according to the equities, and there was no equity in favour of the transferees in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5-B of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, a landowner who fails to reserve or select a permissible area within the prescribed time cannot do so later. The Collector must act judicially, give notice to the landowner and known transferees, hear those who appear, consider their representations, and make a just order. Subject to adjusting the equities, the Collector may place transferred land in either the landowner’s permissible area or surplus area, and may give effect to the landowner’s preference to the extent consistent with those equities.

rule.if: surplus_area_determination_after_owner_failed_to_select_area and transfer_preceded_fixing_area and parties_heard and transferees_did_not_provide_purchase_details and transferees_did_not_oppose_owner_preference

predicates.surplus_area_determination_after_owner_f: The proceeding determined surplus land after the landowner failed to select or reserve a permissible area in time.
predicates.transfer_preceded_fixing_area: The landowner transferred the land before the permissible area was fixed.
predicates.parties_heard: The authority heard the parties who appeared and considered their representations.
predicates.transferees_did_not_provide_purchase_det: The transferees did not provide particulars of the land they had purchased.
predicates.transferees_did_not_oppose_owner_prefere: The transferees did not oppose the landowner’s stated preference for how the transferred land should be allocated.
predicates.transferred_land_not_required_to_be_in_o: The authority is not required to place the transferred land in the landowner’s permissible area.

issues.definition: When a landowner has failed to select a permissible area, land was transferred before that area was fixed, and the transferees did not provide purchase particulars or oppose the landowner’s preference after the parties were heard, the transferees have no automatic entitlement to have the transferred land placed in the permissible area.
